children: Shares of financial advisory firm Perella Weinberg Partners
jumped 12.4% in the morning session after the company reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $251.4 million, representing a 52.7% increase year over year.

According to a company press release, Perella Weinberg Partners reported sequential revenue growth of 61% compared to the second quarter of 2026, while adjusted earnings per share rose to $0.39 from $0.13 in the prior-year period. GAAP diluted earnings per share reached $0.21, with pre-tax profit improving to $35.18 million, or a 14% margin. The firm's quarterly results significantly outperformed Wall Street's expectations, as analysts surveyed by S&P had projected revenue of $182.8 million and adjusted earnings per share of $0.15. The strong top-line acceleration and margin expansion fueled optimism regarding the advisory firm's ongoing profitability.
What is the market telling us

Perella Weinberg’s shares are very volatile and have had 25 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Perella Weinberg and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 15 days ago when the stock dropped 4.2% on the news that September consumer price inflation accelerated to 3.7% and core inflation topped estimates, reigniting concerns over Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.

The hotter-than-expected data showed headline consumer prices rising 3.7% annually, while core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, reached 2.6%. In the wake of the report, traders raised the implied probability of a central bank rate increase at the next meeting to nearly 44%. The sudden shift in policy expectations pushed Treasury yields higher and triggered volatility across bond markets. Banking leaders pointed out that persistent interest rate uncertainty and Treasury market swings are dampening client trading activity and stalling corporate dealmaking as reported by TheStreet. When borrowing costs remain high and unpredictable, corporations typically hold off on mergers, acquisitions, and debt offerings, creating broad sector-wide pressure on investment banking revenue.

Perella Weinberg is down 18.7% since the beginning of the year, and at $14.27 per share, it is trading 41.4% below its 52-week high of $24.34 from February 2026. Despite the year-to-date decline, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Perella Weinberg’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,017.
